columns below - text/bullets in one column and the featured content in the other. This provides better balance and makes charts/tables more readable. Use flexbox with unequal column widths (e.g., 40%/60% split) to optimize space for each content type. 147|- **Full-slide layout**: Let the featured content (chart/table) take up the entire slide for maximum impact and readability 148|- **NEVER vertically stack**: Do not place charts/tables below text in a single column - this causes poor readability and layout issues 149| 150|### Workflow 151|1. **MANDATORY - READ ENTIRE FILE**: Read [`html2pptx.md`](html2pptx.md) completely from start to finish. **NEVER set any range limits when reading this file.** Read the full file content for detailed syntax, critical formatting rules, and best practices before proceeding with presentation creation. 152|2. This involves unpacking the .pptx file, editing the XML content, and repacking it. 174| 175|### Workflow 176|1. **MANDATORY - READ ENTIRE FILE**: Read [`ooxml.md`](ooxml.md) (~500 lines) completely from start to finish. **NEVER set any range limits when reading this file.** Read the full file content for detailed guidance on OOXML structure and editing workflows before any presentation editing. 177|2. Unpack the presentation: `python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py ` 178|3. Edit the XML files (primarily `ppt/slides/slide{N}.xml` and related files) 179|4. **CRITICAL**: Validate immediately after each edit and fix any validation errors before proceeding: `python ooxml/scripts/validate.py --original ` 180|5. Pack the final presentation: `python ooxml/scripts/pack.py ` 181| 182|## Creating a new PowerPoint presentation **using a template** 183| 184|When you need to create a presentation that follows an existing template's design, you'll need to duplicate and re-arrange template slides before then replacing placeholder context. 185| 186|### Workflow 187|1. **Extract template text AND create visual thumbnail grid**: 188| * Extract text: `python -m markitdown template.pptx > template-content.md` 189| * Read `template-content.md`: Read the entire file to understand the contents of the template presentation. **NEVER set any range limits when reading this file.** 190| * Create thumbnail grids: `python scripts/thumbnail.py template.pptx` 191| * See [Creating Thumbnail Grids](#creating-thumbnail-grids) section for more details 192| 193|2. **Analyze template and save inventory to a file**: 194| * **Visual Analysis**: Review thumbnail grid(s) to understand slide layouts, design patterns, and visual structure 195| * Create and save a template inventory file at `template-inventory.md` containing: 196| ```markdown 197| # Template Inventory Analysis 198| **Total Slides: [count]** 199| **IMPORTANT: Slides are 0-indexed (first slide = 0, last slide = count-1)** 200| 201| ## [Category Name] 202| - Slide 0: [Layout code if available] - Description/purpose 203| - Slide 1: [Layout code] - Description/purpose 204| - Slide 2: [Layout code] - Description/purpose 205| [... EVERY slide must be listed individually with its index ...] 206| ``` 207| * **Using the thumbnail grid**: Reference the visual thumbnails to identify: 208| - Layout patterns (title slides, content layouts, section dividers) 209| - Image placeholder locations and counts 210| - Design consistency across slide groups 211| - Visual hierarchy and structure 212| * This inventory file is REQUIRED for selecting appropriate templates in the next step 213| 214|3. **Create presentation outline based on template inventory**: 215| * Review available templates from step 2. 216| * Choose an intro or title template for the first slide. This should be one of the first templates. 217| * Choose safe, text-based layouts for the other slides. 218| * **CRITICAL: Match layout structure to actual content**: 219| - Single-column layouts: Use for unified narrative or single topic 220| - Two-column layouts: Use ONLY when you have exactly 2 distinct items/concepts 221| - Three-column layouts: Use ONLY when you have exactly 3 distinct items/concepts 222| - Image + text layouts: Use ONLY when you have actual images to insert 223| - Quote layouts: Use ONLY for actual quotes from people (with attribution), never for emphasis 224| - Never use layouts with more placeholders than you have content 225| - If you have 2 items, don't force them into a 3-column layout 226| - If you have 4+ items, consider breaking into multiple slides or using a list format 227| * Count your actual content pieces BEFORE selecting the layout 228| * Verify each placeholder in the chosen layout will be filled with meaningful content 229| * Select one option representing the **best** layout for each content section. 230| * Save `outline.md` with content AND template mapping that leverages available designs 231| * Example template mapping: 232| ``` 233| # Template slides to use (0-based indexing) 234| # WARNING: Verify indices are within range! Template with 73 slides has indices 0-72 235| # Mapping: slide numbers from outline -> template slide indices 236| template_mapping = [ 237| 0, # Use slide 0 (Title/Cover) 238| 34, # Use slide 34 (B1: Title and body) 239| 34, # Use slide 34 again (duplicate for second B1) 240| 50, # Use slide 50 (E1: Quote) 241| 54, # Use slide 54 (F2: Closing + Text) 242| ] 243| ``` 244| 245|4. **Duplicate, reorder, and delete slides using `rearrange.py`**: 246| * Use the `scripts/rearrange.py` script to create a new presentation with slides in the desired order: 247| ```bash 248| python scripts/rearrange.py template.pptx working.pptx 0,34,34,50,52 249| ``` 250| * The script handles duplicating repeated slides, deleting unused slides, and reordering automatically 251| * Slide indices are 0-based (first slide is 0, second is 1, etc.) 252| * The same slide index can appear multiple times to duplicate that slide 253| 254|5. **Extract ALL text using the `inventory.py` script**: 255| * **Run inventory extraction**: 256| ```bash 257| python scripts/inventory.py working.pptx text-inventory.json 258| ``` 259| * **Read text-inventory.json**: Read the entire text-inventory.json file to understand all shapes and their properties. **NEVER set any range limits when reading this file.** 260| 261| * The inventory JSON structure: 262| ```json 263| { 264| "slide-0": { 265| "shape-0": { 266| "placeholder_type": "TITLE", // or null for non-placeholders 267| "left": 1.5, // position in inches 268| "top": 2.0, 269| "width": 7.5, 270| "height": 1.2, 271| "paragraphs": [ 272| { 273| "text": "Paragraph text", 274| // Optional properties (only included when non-default): 275| "bullet": true, // explicit bullet detected 276| "level": 0, // only included when bullet is true 277| "alignment": "CENTER", // CENTER, RIGHT (not LEFT) 278| "space_before": 10.0, // space before paragraph in points 279| "space_after": 6.0, // space after paragraph in points 280| "line_spacing": 22.4, // line spacing in points 281| "font_name": "Arial", // from first run 282| "font_size": 14.0, // in points 283| "bold": true, 284| "italic": false, 285| "underline": false, 286| "color": "FF0000" // RGB color 287| } 288| ] 289| } 290| } 291| } 292| ``` 293| 294| * Key features: 295| - **Slides**: Named as "slide-0", "slide-1", etc. 296| - **Shapes**: Ordered by visual position (top-to-bottom, left-to-right) as "shape-0", "shape-1", etc. 297| - **Placeholder types**: TITLE, CENTER_TITLE, SUBTITLE, BODY, OBJECT, or null 298| - **Default font size**: `default_font_size` in points extracted from layout placeholders (when available) 299| - **Slide numbers are filtered**: Shapes with SLIDE_NUMBER placeholder type are automatically excluded from inventory 300| - **Bullets**: When `bullet: true`, `level` is always included (even if 0) 301| - **Spacing**: `space_before`, `space_after`, and `line_spacing` in points (only included when set) 302| - **Colors**: `color` for RGB (e.g., "FF0000"), `theme_color` for theme colors (e.g., "DARK_1") 303| - **Properties**: Only non-default values are included in the output 304| 305|6. **Generate replacement text and save the data to a JSON file** 306| Based on the text inventory from the previous step: 307| - **CRITICAL**: First verify which shapes exist in the inventory - only reference shapes that are actually present 308| - **VALIDATION**: The replace.py script will validate that all shapes in your replacement JSON exist in the inventory 309| - If you reference a non-existent shape, you'll get an error showing available shapes 310| - If you reference a non-existent slide, you'll get an error indicating the slide doesn't exist 311| - All validation errors are shown at once before the script exits 312| - **IMPORTANT**: The replace.py script uses inventory.py internally to identify ALL text shapes 313| - **AUTOMATIC CLEARING**: ALL text shapes from the inventory will be cleared unless you provide "paragraphs" for them 314| - Add a "paragraphs" field to shapes that need content (not "replacement_paragraphs") 315| - Shapes without "paragraphs" in the replacement JSON will have their text cleared automatically 316| - Paragraphs with bullets will be automatically left aligned. Don't set the `alignment` property on when `"bullet": true` 317| - Generate appropriate replacement content for placeholder text 318| - Use shape size to determine appropriate content length 319| - **CRITICAL**: Include paragraph properties from the original inventory - don't just provide text 320| - **IMPORTANT**: When bullet: true, do NOT include bullet symbols (•, -, *) in text - they're added automatically 321| - **ESSENTIAL FORMATTING RULES**: 322| - Headers/titles should typically have `"bold": true` 323| - List items should have `"bullet": true, "level": 0` (level is required when bullet is true) 324| - Preserve any alignment properties (e.g., `"alignment": "CENTER"` for centered text) 325| - Include font properties when different from default (e.g., `"font_size": 14.0`, `"font_name": "Lora"`) 326| - Colors: Use `"color": "FF0000"` for RGB or `"theme_color": "DARK_1"` for theme colors 327| - The replacement script expects **properly formatted paragraphs**, not just text strings 328| - **Overlapping shapes**: Prefer shapes with larger default_font_size or more appropriate placeholder_type 329| - Save the updated inventory with replacements to `replacement-text.json` 330| - **WARNING**: Different template layouts have different shape counts - always check the actual inventory before creating replacements 331| 332| Example paragraphs field showing proper formatting: 333| ```json 334| "paragraphs": [ 335| { 336| "text": "New presentation title text", 337| "alignment": "CENTER", 338| "bold": true 339| }, 340| { 341| "text": "Section Header", 342| "bold": true 343| }, 344| { 345| "text": "First bullet point without bullet symbol", 346| "bullet": true, 347| "level": 0 348| }, 349| { 350| "text": "Red colored text", 351| "color": "FF0000" 352| }, 353| { 354| "text": "Theme colored text", 355| "theme_color": "DARK_1" 356| }, 357| { 358| "text": "Regular paragraph text without special formatting" 359| } 360| ] 361| ``` 362| 363| **Shapes not listed in the replacement JSON are automatically cleared**: 364| ```json 365| { 366| "slide-0": { 367| "shape-0": { 368| "paragraphs": [...] // This shape gets new text 369| } 370| // shape-1 and shape-2 from inventory will be cleared automatically 371| } 372| } 373| ``` 374| 375| **Common formatting patterns for presentations**: 376| - Title slides: Bold text, sometimes centered 377| - Section headers within slides: Bold text 378| - Bullet lists: Each item needs `"bullet": true, "level": 0` 379| - Body text: Usually no special properties needed 380| - Quotes: May have special alignment or font properties 381| 382|7. **Apply replacements using the `replace.py` script** 383| ```bash 384| python scripts/replace.py working.pptx replacement-text.json output.pptx 385| ``` 386| 387| The script will: 388| - First extract the inventory of ALL text shapes using functions from inventory.py 389| - Validate that all shapes in the replacement JSON exist in the inventory 390| - Clear text from ALL shapes identified in the inventory 391| - Apply new text only to shapes with "paragraphs" defined in the replacement JSON 392| - Preserve formatting by applying paragraph properties from the JSON 393| - Handle bullets, alignment, font properties, and colors automatically 394| - Save the updated presentation 395| 396| Example validation errors: 397| ``` 398| ERROR: Invalid shapes in replacement JSON: 399| - Shape 'shape-99' not found on 'slide-0'. Available shapes: shape-0, shape-1, shape-4 400| - Slide 'slide-999' not found in inventory 401| ``` 402| 403| ``` 404| ERROR: Replacement text made overflow worse in these shapes: 405| - slide-0/shape-2: overflow worsened by 1.25" (was 0.00", now 1.25") 406| ``` 407| 408|## Creating Thumbnail Grids 409| 410|To create visual thumbnail grids of PowerPoint slides for quick analysis and reference: 411| 412|```bash 413|python scripts/thumbnail.py template.pptx [output_prefix] 414|``` 415| 416|**Features**: 417|- Creates: `thumbnails.jpg` (or `thumbnails-1.jpg`, `thumbnails-2.jpg`, etc. for large decks) 418|- Default: 5 columns, max 30 slides per grid (5×6) 419|- Custom prefix: `python scripts/thumbnail.py template.pptx my-grid` 420| - Note: The output prefix should include the path if you want output in a specific directory (e.g., `workspace/my-grid`) 421|- Adjust columns: `--cols 4` (range: 3-6, affects slides per grid) 422|- Grid limits: 3 cols = 12 slides/grid, 4 cols = 20, 5 cols = 30, 6 cols = 42 423|- Slides are zero-indexed (Slide 0, Slide 1, etc.) 424| 425|**Use cases**: 426|- Template analysis: Quickly understand slide layouts and design patterns 427|- Content review: Visual overview of entire presentation 428|- Navigation reference: Find specific slides by their visual appearance 429|- Quality check: Verify all slides are properly formatted 430| 431|**Examples**: 432|```bash 433|# Basic usage 434|python scripts/thumbnail.py presentation.pptx 435| 436|# Combine options: custom name, columns 437|python scripts/thumbnail.py template.pptx analysis --cols 4 438|``` 439| 440|## Converting Slides to Images 441| 442|To visually analyze PowerPoint slides, convert them to images using a two-step process: 443| 444|1. **Convert PPTX to PDF**: 445| ```bash 446| soffice --headless --convert-to pdf template.pptx 447| ``` 448| 449|2. **Convert PDF pages to JPEG images**: 450| ```bash 451| pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 template.pdf slide 452| ``` 453| This creates files like `slide-1.jpg`, `slide-2.jpg`, etc. 454| 455|Options: 456|- `-r 150`: Sets resolution to 150 DPI (adjust for quality/size balance) 457|- `-jpeg`: Output JPEG format (use `-png` for PNG if preferred) 458|- `-f N`: First page to convert (e.g., `-f 2` starts from page 2) 459|- `-l N`: Last page to convert (e.g., `-l 5` stops at page 5) 460|- `slide`: Prefix for output files {"code": "from __future__ import annotations

import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import time
import math
from lxml import etree

BASE_DIR = Path("/tmp/pptx_reference_formatting")
pptx_path = Path("/home/liangfeng/git/hermes-agent/benchmark/skillsbench/tasks/pptx-reference-formatting/environment/Awesome-Agent-Papers.pptx")
output_pptx = BASE_DIR / "Awesome-Agent-Papers_processed.pptx"
unpack_dir = BASE_DIR / "unpacked"
skills_ooxml = Path("/home/liangfeng/git/hermes-agent/benchmark/skillsbench/tasks/pptx-reference-formatting/environment/skills/pptx/ooxml")

pack_script = skills_ooxml / "scripts" / "pack.py"
validate_script = skills_ooxml / "scripts" / "validate.py"

NS = {
    "a": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main",
    "p": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/presentationml/2006/main",
    "r": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships"
}

def looks_like_title(text: str) -> bool:
    t = " ".join(text.split())
    if len(t) < 15 or len(t) > 160:
        return False
    lowered = t.lower()
    if any(token in lowered for token in ["http://", "https://", "www.", "doi", "arxiv"]):
        return False
    if re.search(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", t):
        return False
    # Quoted titles are strong signals
    if re.search(r"[\"""].+[\""""]", t):
        return True
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-]*", t)
    if len(words) < 4 or len(words) > 20:
        return False
    title_case_ratio = sum(1 for w in words if w[0].isupper()) / len(words)
    if title_case_ratio >= 0.6:
        return True
    if (":" in t or " - " in t) and title_case_ratio >= 0.5:
        return True
    return False

def apply_style_to_rpr(rpr: etree._Element) -> None:
    rpr.set("sz", "1600")
    rpr.set("dirty", "0")
    rpr.set("b", "0")

    solid_fill = rpr.find("a:solidFill", NS)
    if solid_fill is None:
        solid_fill = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}solidFill")
        rpr.insert(0, solid_fill)
    else:
        for child in list(solid_fill):
            solid_fill.remove(child)

    srgb = etree.SubElement(solid_fill, f"{{{NS['a']}}}srgbClr")
    srgb.set("val", "989596")

    latin = rpr.find("a:latin", NS)
    if latin is None:
        latin = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{NS['a']}}}latin")
    latin.set("typeface", "Arial")

    ea = rpr.find("a:ea", NS)
    if ea is None:
        ea = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{NS['a']}}}ea")
    ea.set("typeface", "Arial")

    cs = rpr.find("a:cs", NS)
    if cs is None:
        cs = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{NS['a']}}}cs")
    cs.set("typeface", "Arial")

def apply_style_to_paragraph(paragraph: etree._Element) -> int:
    changed = 0
    ppr = paragraph.find("a:pPr", NS)
    if ppr is None:
        ppr = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}pPr")
        paragraph.insert(0, ppr)
    ppr.set("algn", "ctr")

    for run in paragraph.findall("a:r", NS):
        rpr = run.find("a:rPr", NS)
        if rpr is None:
            rpr = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}rPr")
            first_child = run.find("a:t", NS)
            if first_child is not None:
                run.insert(run.index(first_child), rpr)
            else:
                run.insert(0, rpr)
        apply_style_to_rpr(rpr)
        changed += 1
    end_rpr = paragraph.find("a:endParaRPr", NS)
    if end_rpr is not None:
        apply_style_to_rpr(end_rpr)
    return changed

def get_paragraph_text(paragraph: etree._Element) -> str:
    return "".join(paragraph.xpath(".//a:t/text()", namespaces=NS))

def get_slide_dimensions(unpack_dir: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    presentation_path = unpack_dir / "ppt" / "presentation.xml"
    pres_tree = etree.parse(str(presentation_path))
    pres_root = pres_tree.getroot()
    sld_sz = pres_root.find(".//p:sldSz", NS)
    if sld_sz is not None:
        width = int(sld_sz.get("cx"))
        height = int(sld_sz.get("cy"))
        return width, height
    raise RuntimeError("Slide size (sldSz) not found in presentation.xml")

def adjust_shape_position_and_size(paragraph: etree._Element, slide_width: int, slide_height: int) -> bool:
    shape = paragraph
    while shape is not None:
        if shape.tag.endswith("}sp"):
            break
        shape = shape.getparent()
    if shape is None:
        return False

    sp_pr = shape.find("p:spPr", NS)
    if sp_pr is None:
        return False

    xfrm = sp_pr.find("a:xfrm", NS)
    if xfrm is None:
        xfrm = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}xfrm")
        sp_pr.insert(0, xfrm)

    off = xfrm.find("a:off", NS)
    if off is None:
        off = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}off")
        ext_elem = xfrm.find("a:ext", NS)
        if ext_elem is not None:
            xfrm.insert(xfrm.index(ext_elem), off)
        else:
            xfrm.insert(0, off)

    ext = xfrm.find("a:ext", NS)
    if ext is None:
        ext = etree.SubElement(xfrm, f"{{{NS['a']}}}ext")

    font_size_hundreth_pt = 1600
    first_run = paragraph.find(".//a:r", NS)
    if first_run is not None:
        rpr = first_run.find("a:rPr", NS)
        if rpr is not None and "sz" in rpr.attrib:
            font_size_hundreth_pt = int(rpr.get("sz"))

    font_height_emu = font_size_hundreth_pt * 127
    shape_width = slide_width
    shape_height = int(font_height_emu * 1.3)

    ext.set("cx", str(shape_width))
    ext.set("cy", str(shape_height))

    x_pos = 0
    margin_bottom = int(0.01 * slide_height)
    y_pos = slide_height - shape_height - margin_bottom

    off.set("x", str(x_pos))
    off.set("y", str(y_pos))

    # Also set bodyPr to ensure center alignment
    tx_body = shape.find("p:txBody", NS)
    if tx_body is not None:
        body_pr = tx_body.find("a:bodyPr", NS)
        if body_pr is None:
            body_pr = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}bodyPr")
            tx_body.insert(0, body_pr)
        body_pr.set("lIns", "0")
        body_pr.set("rIns", "0")

    return True

def process_slides(unpack_dir: Path, slide_width: int, slide_height: int) -> tuple[int, int, list[str]]:
    slides_dir = unpack_dir / "ppt" / "slides"
    slide_files = sorted(slides_dir.glob("slide*.xml"))
    total_titles = 0
    total_runs = 0
    collected_titles = []
    seen = set()

    for slide_path in slide_files:
        tree = etree.parse(str(slide_path))
        root = tree.getroot()
        slide_changed = False
        for paragraph in root.xpath(".//a:p", namespaces=NS):
            text = get_paragraph_text(paragraph)
            if looks_like_title(text):
                print(f"Found title on {slide_path.name}: {text[:60]}...")

                text_normalized = " ".join(text.split())
                if text_normalized not in seen:
                    seen.add(text_normalized)
                    collected_titles.append(text_normalized)

                changed_runs = apply_style_to_paragraph(paragraph)
                positioned = adjust_shape_position_and_size(paragraph, slide_width, slide_height)
                if changed_runs or positioned:
                    slide_changed = True
                    total_titles += 1
                    total_runs += changed_runs
        if slide_changed:
            tree.write(str(slide_path), xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone="yes")

    return total_titles, total_runs, collected_titles

# Main execution
print("Starting main processing...")
slide_width, slide_height = get_slide_dimensions(unpack_dir)
print(f"Slide dimensions: {slide_width} x {slide_height} EMUs")

# Process slides
total_titles, total_runs, collected_titles = process_slides(unpack_dir, slide_width, slide_height)
print(f"Processed {total_titles} title instances, {total_runs} runs, found {len(collected_titles)} unique titles")

# Print collected titles for verification
for i, t in enumerate(collected_titles):
    print(f"  {i+1}. {t}")
"}

    if len(words) < 4 or len(words) > 20:
        return False
    title_case_ratio = sum(1 for w in words if w[0].isupper()) / len(words)
    if title_case_ratio >= 0.6:
        return True
    if (":" in t or " - " in t) and title_case_ratio >= 0.5:
        return True
    return False

def apply_style_to_rpr(rpr: etree._Element) -> None:
    rpr.set("sz", "1600")
    rpr.set("dirty", "0")
    rpr.set("b", "0")

    solid_fill = rpr.find("a:solidFill", NS)
    if solid_fill is None:
        solid_fill = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}solidFill")
        rpr.insert(0, solid_fill)
    else:
        for child in list(solid_fill):
            solid_fill.remove(child)

    srgb = etree.SubElement(solid_fill, f"{{{NS['a']}}}srgbClr")
    srgb.set("val", "989596")

    latin = rpr.find("a:latin", NS)
    if latin is None:
        latin = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{NS['a']}}}latin")
    latin.set("typeface", "Arial")

    ea = rpr.find("a:ea", NS)
    if ea is None:
        ea = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{NS['a']}}}ea")
    ea.set("typeface", "Arial")

    cs = rpr.find("a:cs", NS)
    if cs is None:
        cs = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{NS['a']}}}cs")
    cs.set("typeface", "Arial")

def apply_style_to_paragraph(paragraph: etree._Element) -> int:
    changed = 0
    ppr = paragraph.find("a:pPr", NS)
    if ppr is None:
        ppr = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}pPr")
        paragraph.insert(0, ppr)
    ppr.set("algn", "ctr")

    for run in paragraph.findall("a:r", NS):
        rpr = run.find("a:rPr", NS)
        if rpr is None:
            rpr = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}rPr")
            first_child = run.find("a:t", NS)
            if first_child is not None:
                run.insert(run.index(first_child), rpr)
            else:
                run.insert(0, rpr)
        apply_style_to_rpr(rpr)
        changed += 1
    end_rpr = paragraph.find("a:endParaRPr", NS)
    if end_rpr is not None:
        apply_style_to_rpr(end_rpr)
    return changed

def get_paragraph_text(paragraph: etree._Element) -> str:
    return "".join(paragraph.xpath(".//a:t/text()", namespaces=NS))

def get_slide_dimensions(unpack_dir: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    presentation_path = unpack_dir / "ppt" / "presentation.xml"
    pres_tree = etree.parse(str(presentation_path))
    pres_root = pres_tree.getroot()
    sld_sz = pres_root.find(".//p:sldSz", NS)
    if sld_sz is not None:
        width = int(sld_sz.get("cx"))
        height = int(sld_sz.get("cy"))
        return width, height
    raise RuntimeError("Slide size (sldSz) not found in presentation.xml")

def adjust_shape_position_and_size(paragraph: etree._Element, slide_width: int, slide_height: int) -> bool:
    shape = paragraph
    while shape is not None:
        if shape.tag.endswith("}sp"):
            break
        shape = shape.getparent()
    if shape is None:
        return False

    sp_pr = shape.find("p:spPr", NS)
    if sp_pr is None:
        return False

    xfrm = sp_pr.find("a:xfrm", NS)
    if xfrm is None:
        xfrm = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}xfrm")
        sp_pr.insert(0, xfrm)

    off = xfrm.find("a:off", NS)
    if off is None:
        off = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}off")
        ext_elem = xfrm.find("a:ext", NS)
        if ext_elem is not None:
            xfrm.insert(xfrm.index(ext_elem), off)
        else:
            xfrm.insert(0, off)

    ext = xfrm.find("a:ext", NS)
    if ext is None:
        ext = etree.SubElement(xfrm, f"{{{NS['a']}}}ext")

    font_size_hundreth_pt = 1600
    first_run = paragraph.find(".//a:r", NS)
    if first_run is not None:
        rpr = first_run.find("a:rPr", NS)
        if rpr is not None and "sz" in rpr.attrib:
            font_size_hundreth_pt = int(rpr.get("sz"))

    font_height_emu = font_size_hundreth_pt * 127
    shape_width = slide_width
    shape_height = int(font_height_emu * 1.3)

    ext.set("cx", str(shape_width))
    ext.set("cy", str(shape_height))

    x_pos = 0
    margin_bottom = int(0.01 * slide_height)
    y_pos = slide_height - shape_height - margin_bottom

    off.set("x", str(x_pos))
    off.set("y", str(y_pos))

    # Also set bodyPr to ensure center alignment
    tx_body = shape.find("p:txBody", NS)
    if tx_body is not None:
        body_pr = tx_body.find("a:bodyPr", NS)
        if body_pr is None:
            body_pr = etree.Element(f"{{{NS['a']}}}bodyPr")
            tx_body.insert(0, body_pr)
        body_pr.set("lIns", "0")
        body_pr.set("rIns", "0")

    return True

def process_slides(unpack_dir: Path, slide_width: int, slide_height: int) -> tuple[int, int, list[str]]:
    slides_dir = unpack_dir / "ppt" / "slides"
    slide_files = sorted(slides_dir.glob("slide*.xml"))
    total_titles = 0
    total_runs = 0
    collected_titles = []
    seen = set()

    for slide_path in slide_files:
        tree = etree.parse(str(slide_path))
        root = tree.getroot()
        slide_changed = False
        for paragraph in root.xpath(".//a:p", namespaces=NS):
            text = get_paragraph_text(paragraph)
            if looks_like_title(text):
                print(f"Found title on {slide_path.name}: {text[:80]}...")

                text_normalized = " ".join(text.split())
                if text_normalized not in seen:
                    seen.add(text_normalized)
                    collected_titles.append(text_normalized)

                changed_runs = apply_style_to_paragraph(paragraph)
                positioned = adjust_shape_position_and_size(paragraph, slide_width, slide_height)
                if changed_runs or positioned:
                    slide_changed = True
                    total_titles += 1
                    total_runs += changed_runs
        if slide_changed:
            tree.write(str(slide_path), xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone="yes")

    return total_titles, total_runs, collected_titles

# Main execution
print("Starting main processing...")
slide_width, slide_height = get_slide_dimensions(unpack_dir)
print(f"Slide dimensions: {slide_width} x {slide_height} EMUs")

# Process slides
total_titles, total_runs, collected_titles = process_slides(unpack_dir, slide_width, slide_height)
print(f"Processed {total_titles} title instances, {total_runs} runs, found {len(collected_titles)} unique titles")

# Print collected titles for verification
for i, t in enumerate(collected_titles):
    print(f"  {i+1}. {t}")
"}

# SkillsBench

Benchmark for evaluating how well AI agents use skills. 89 tasks, working toward 100+.

## Python environment (Hermes monorepo)

This directory is a **nested Python package** (`skillsbench` in `pyproject.toml`; `requires-python >= 3.12`). Hermes itself supports Python 3.11+, but use **3.12+** when developing or running BenchFlow workflows here.

- **Same venv as Hermes, BenchFlow only:** from the Hermes repo root, `pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"` (or `uv pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"`). That pulls in `benchflow` via the root `hermes-agent` optional extra; it does not install the `skillsbench` package in editable mode.
- **Full subproject:** `cd benchmark/skillsbench` then `pip install -e .` or `uv sync` (see `pyproject.toml` for dev groups and `uv` sources).

## Commands

```bash
pip install benchflow>=0.3.0a7
bench tasks init <task-name>
bench tasks check tasks/<task-id>
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a oracle
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp -s tasks/<task-id>/environment/skills/  # with skills
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp  # without skills
bench job -t tasks/ -a claude-agent-acp -e daytona -c 8
bench metrics jobs/<run-dir>
bench skills list
bench skills eval --help
```

## Task Layout

```
tasks/<task-id>/
  instruction.md          # Human-written. Outcome-focused. No skill hints.
  task.toml               # Metadata, timeouts, resources
  environment/
    Dockerfile            # Container setup
    skills/               # Domain skills (generalizable, not task-specific)
  solution/
    solve.sh              # Oracle (human-written, derives answers via computation)
  tests/
    test.sh               # Pytest runner, writes reward.txt
    test_outputs.py       # Outcome-based assertions
```

## Rules

- instruction.md, solve.sh, and task.toml must be human-written — never generate these
- Never mention skill names in instructions
- Skills must be generalizable and reusable, not task-specific
- Tests verify outcomes, not process — don't check which tools were used
- Oracle must derive answers through computation, not hardcode them
- No fake scenarios, no synthetic data when real data exists
- Prefer tasks without external API dependencies

## Key References

- [../../AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) — Hermes repo guide; **Development Environment → SkillsBench: Hermes batch driver** documents `benchmark/scripts/run_skillsbench_with_hermes.py` (defaults, examples, flags).
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — full contributor guide, rubrics, authorship policy
- [rubrics/](rubrics/) — task proposal and implementation review criteria
- [.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md) — how to write skills
- [docs/unit-test-guidelines.md](docs/unit-test-guidelines.md) — test statistics and patterns

print(f"Target samples ({len(target_samples)}): {target_samples}")

# (Excel formulas for cross-sheet lookup would be INDEX(Data!B1:BA201, MATCH(...), MATCH(...)))
# But the instruction says "Use formulas, not hard-coded numbers"
# Let's use Excel INDEX+MATCH formulas

for row_idx, prot_id in enumerate(target_proteins, 11):
    for col_idx, sample_name in enumerate(target_samples, 3):
        # Excel formula: use INDEX + MATCH
        # INDEX(array, MATCH(lookup_value, lookup_array, 0))
        # The array = Data!$A$2:$BA$201 (but we need value columns 2:53 for samples)

    task_ws.cell(row=26, column=2+p_idx, value=f'=AVERAGE({treat_range})')          # Treated Mean
    task_ws.cell(row=27, column=2+p_idx, value=f'=STDEV.S({treat_range})')          # Treated StdDev

print("Step 2: Statistics formulas filled in rows 24-27, cols B-K")

# Step 3: Fold changes in C-D, rows 32-41

    # Log2 FC: =B26-B24 but we need column reference
    ctrl_mean_ref = f'{col_stats}24'

    # Log2FC = Treated Mean - Control Mean
    task_ws.cell(row=row, column=4, value=f'={treat_mean_ref}-{ctrl_mean_ref}')  # Log2FC in col D
    
    # FC = 2^(Log2FC)
    task_ws.cell(row=row, column=3, value=f'=2^D{row}')  # Fold Change in col C

print("Step 3: Fold change formulas filled in rows 32-41, cols C and D")

# Save the workbook

print("Workbook saved with formulas")

{"code": "import openpyxl
import statistics as stats
import shutil

wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('/tmp/protein_expression.xlsx')
task_ws = wb['Task']
data_ws = wb['Data']

# Helper: find protein row in Data sheet
def find_protein_row(data_ws, protein_id):
    for row in range(2, data_ws.max_row + 1):
        if data_ws.cell(row=row, column=1).value == protein_id:
            return row
    return None

# Step 1: Lookup and fill expression values
target_proteins = []
for row in range(11, 21):
    prot_id = task_ws.cell(row=row, column=1).value
    if prot_id:
        target_proteins.append(prot_id)

target_samples = []
for col in range(3, 13):
    sample_name = task_ws.cell(row=10, column=col).value
    if sample_name:
        target_samples.append(sample_name)

# Find sample column index in Data sheet
def find_sample_col(data_ws, sample_name):
    for col in range(1, data_ws.max_column + 1):
        if data_ws.cell(row=1, column=col).value == sample_name:
            return col
    return None

# Fill values directly
for r_idx, prot_id in enumerate(target_proteins, 11):
    prow = find_protein_row(data_ws, prot_id)
    if prow is None:
        continue
    for c_idx, sample_name in enumerate(target_samples, 3):
        scol = find_sample_col(data_ws, sample_name)
        if scol:
            val = data_ws.cell(row=prow, column=scol).value
            task_ws.cell(row=r_idx, column=c_idx, value=val)

print("Step 1 filled: 10 proteins x 10 samples")

# Step 2: Calculate statistics
# From Data sheet row 1, find which are control vs treated
# We know from Task row 9: C-G = Control, H-L = Treated
control_sample_names = []
treated_sample_names = []
for col in range(3, 13):
    group = task_ws.cell(row=9, column=col).value
    if group == 'Control':
        control_sample_names.append(task_ws.cell(row=10, column=col).value)
    elif group == 'Treated':
        treated_sample_names.append(task_ws.cell(row=10, column=col).value)

print(f"Control: {control_sample_names}")
print(f"Treated: {treated_sample_names}")

for p_idx, prot_id in enumerate(target_proteins):
    prow = find_protein_row(data_ws, prot_id)
    if prow is None:
        continue
    
    ctrl_vals = []
    treat_vals = []
    
    for col in range(1, data_ws.max_column + 1):
        sample_name = data_ws.cell(row=1, column=col).value
        value = data_ws.cell(row=prow, column=col).value
        if value is None:
            continue
        if sample_name in control_sample_names:
            ctrl_vals.append(float(value))
        elif sample_name in treated_sample_names:
            treat_vals.append(float(value))
    
    ctrl_mean = round(stats.mean(ctrl_vals), 3) if ctrl_vals else 0
    ctrl_std = round(stats.stdev(ctrl_vals), 3) if len(ctrl_vals) > 1 else 0
    treat_mean = round(stats.mean(treat_vals), 3) if treat_vals else 0
    treat_std = round(stats.stdev(treat_vals), 3) if len(treat_vals) > 1 else 0
    
    col_idx = 2 + p_idx  # Column B-K
    task_ws.cell(row=24, column=col_idx, value=ctrl_mean)
    task_ws.cell(row=25, column=col_idx, value=ctrl_std)
    task_ws.cell(row=26, column=col_idx, value=treat_mean)
    task_ws.cell(row=27, column=col_idx, value=treat_std)

print(f"Step 2 done: stats for {len(target_proteins)} proteins")

# Step 3: Fold change calculations
for p_idx in range(10):
    row = 32 + p_idx
    col_stats = 2 + p_idx  # Column B-K
    
    prot_id = target_proteins[p_idx]
    gene = task_ws.cell(row=11 + p_idx, column=2).value
    
    task_ws.cell(row=row, column=1, value=prot_id)
    task_ws.cell(row=row, column=2, value=gene)
    
    ctrl_mean = task_ws.cell(row=24, column=col_stats).value or 0
    treat_mean = task_ws.cell(row=26, column=col_stats).value or 0
    
    log2fc = treat_mean - ctrl_mean
    fc = 2 ** log2fc
    
    task_ws.cell(row=row, column=3, value=round(fc, 3))    # Fold Change in C
    task_ws.cell(row=row, column=4, value=round(log2fc, 3)) # Log2FC in D

print(f"Step 3 done: fold changes for 10 proteins")

wb.save('/tmp/protein_expression.xlsx')
print("Saved!")
"}

# SkillsBench

Benchmark for evaluating how well AI agents use skills. 89 tasks, working toward 100+.

## Python environment (Hermes monorepo)

This directory is a **nested Python package** (`skillsbench` in `pyproject.toml`; `requires-python >= 3.12`). Hermes itself supports Python 3.11+, but use **3.12+** when developing or running BenchFlow workflows here.

- **Same venv as Hermes, BenchFlow only:** from the Hermes repo root, `pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"` (or `uv pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"`). That pulls in `benchflow` via the root `hermes-agent` optional extra; it does not install the `skillsbench` package in editable mode.
- **Full subproject:** `cd benchmark/skillsbench` then `pip install -e .` or `uv sync` (see `pyproject.toml` for dev groups and `uv` sources).

## Commands

```bash
pip install benchflow>=0.3.0a7
bench tasks init <task-name>
bench tasks check tasks/<task-id>
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a oracle
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp -s tasks/<task-id>/environment/skills/  # with skills
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp  # without skills
bench job -t tasks/ -a claude-agent-acp -e daytona -c 8
bench metrics jobs/<run-dir>
bench skills list
bench skills eval --help
```

## Task Layout

```
tasks/<task-id>/
  instruction.md          # Human-written. Outcome-focused. No skill hints.
  task.toml               # Metadata, timeouts, resources
  environment/
    Dockerfile            # Container setup
    skills/               # Domain skills (generalizable, not task-specific)
  solution/
    solve.sh              # Oracle (human-written, derives answers via computation)
  tests/
    test.sh               # Pytest runner, writes reward.txt
    test_outputs.py       # Outcome-based assertions
```

## Rules

- instruction.md, solve.sh, and task.toml must be human-written — never generate these
- Never mention skill names in instructions
- Skills must be generalizable and reusable, not task-specific
- Tests verify outcomes, not process — don't check which tools were used
- Oracle must derive answers through computation, not hardcode them
- No fake scenarios, no synthetic data when real data exists
- Prefer tasks without external API dependencies

## Key References

- [../../AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) — Hermes repo guide; **Development Environment → SkillsBench: Hermes batch driver** documents `benchmark/scripts/run_skillsbench_with_hermes.py` (defaults, examples, flags).
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — full contributor guide, rubrics, authorship policy
- [rubrics/](rubrics/) — task proposal and implementation review criteria
- [.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md) — how to write skills
- [docs/unit-test-guidelines.md](docs/unit-test-guidelines.md) — test statistics and patterns

# SkillsBench

Benchmark for evaluating how well AI agents use skills. 89 tasks, working toward 100+.

## Python environment (Hermes monorepo)

This directory is a **nested Python package** (`skillsbench` in `pyproject.toml`; `requires-python >= 3.12`). Hermes itself supports Python 3.11+, but use **3.12+** when developing or running BenchFlow workflows here.

- **Same venv as Hermes, BenchFlow only:** from the Hermes repo root, `pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"` (or `uv pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"`). That pulls in `benchflow` via the root `hermes-agent` optional extra; it does not install the `skillsbench` package in editable mode.
- **Full subproject:** `cd benchmark/skillsbench` then `pip install -e .` or `uv sync` (see `pyproject.toml` for dev groups and `uv` sources).

## Commands

```bash
pip install benchflow>=0.3.0a7
bench tasks init <task-name>
bench tasks check tasks/<task-id>
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a oracle
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp -s tasks/<task-id>/environment/skills/  # with skills
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp  # without skills
bench job -t tasks/ -a claude-agent-acp -e daytona -c 8
bench metrics jobs/<run-dir>
bench skills list
bench skills eval --help
```

## Task Layout

```
tasks/<task-id>/
  instruction.md          # Human-written. Outcome-focused. No skill hints.
  task.toml               # Metadata, timeouts, resources
  environment/
    Dockerfile            # Container setup
    skills/               # Domain skills (generalizable, not task-specific)
  solution/
    solve.sh              # Oracle (human-written, derives answers via computation)
  tests/
    test.sh               # Pytest runner, writes reward.txt
    test_outputs.py       # Outcome-based assertions
```

## Rules

- instruction.md, solve.sh, and task.toml must be human-written — never generate these
- Never mention skill names in instructions
- Skills must be generalizable and reusable, not task-specific
- Tests verify outcomes, not process — don't check which tools were used
- Oracle must derive answers through computation, not hardcode them
- No fake scenarios, no synthetic data when real data exists
- Prefer tasks without external API dependencies

## Key References

- [../../AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) — Hermes repo guide; **Development Environment → SkillsBench: Hermes batch driver** documents `benchmark/scripts/run_skillsbench_with_hermes.py` (defaults, examples, flags).
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — full contributor guide, rubrics, authorship policy
- [rubrics/](rubrics/) — task proposal and implementation review criteria
- [.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md) — how to write skills
- [docs/unit-test-guidelines.md](docs/unit-test-guidelines.md) — test statistics and patterns

{"content": "     1|---
     2|name: qutip
     3|description: "Quantum mechanics simulations and analysis using QuTiP (Quantum Toolbox in Python). Use when working with quantum systems including: (1) quantum states (kets, bras, density matrices), (2) quantum operators and gates, (3) time evolution and dynamics (Schrödinger, master equations, Monte Carlo), (4) open quantum systems with dissipation, (5) quantum measurements and entanglement, (6) visualization (Bloch sphere, Wigner functions), (7) steady states and correlation functions, or (8) advanced methods (Floquet theory, HEOM, stochastic solvers). Handles both closed and open quantum systems across various domains including quantum optics, quantum computing, and condensed matter physics."
     4|---
     5|
     6|# QuTiP: Quantum Toolbox in Python
     7|
     8|## Overview
     9|
    10|QuTiP provides comprehensive tools for simulating and analyzing quantum mechanical systems. It handles both closed (unitary) and open (dissipative) quantum systems with multiple solvers optimized for different scenarios.
    11|
    12|## Installation
    13|
    14|```bash
    15|uv pip install qutip
    16|```
    17|
    18|Optional packages for additional functionality:
    19|
    20|```bash
    21|# Quantum information processing (circuits, gates)
    22|uv pip install qutip-qip
    23|
    24|# Quantum trajectory viewer
    25|uv pip install qutip-qtrl
    26|```
    27|
    28|## Quick Start
    29|
    30|```python
    31|from qutip import *
    32|import numpy as np
    33|import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    34|
    35|# Create quantum state
    36|psi = basis(2, 0)  # |0⟩ state
    37|
    38|# Create operator
    39|H = sigmaz()  # Hamiltonian
    40|
    41|# Time evolution
    42|tlist = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
    43|result = sesolve(H, psi, tlist, e_ops=[sigmaz()])
    44|
    45|# Plot results
    46|plt.plot(tlist, result.expect[0])
    47|plt.xlabel('Time')
    48|plt.ylabel('⟨σz⟩')
    49|plt.show()
    50|```
    51|
    52|## Core Capabilities
    53|
    54|### 1. Quantum Objects and States
    55|
    56|Create and manipulate quantum states and operators:
    57|
    58|```python
    59|# States
    60|psi = basis(N, n)  # Fock state |n⟩
    61|psi = coherent(N, alpha)  # Coherent state |α⟩
    62|rho = thermal_dm(N, n_avg)  # Thermal density matrix
    63|
    64|# Operators
    65|a = destroy(N)  # Annihilation operator
    66|H = num(N)  # Number operator
    67|sx, sy, sz = sigmax(), sigmay(), sigmaz()  # Pauli matrices
    68|
    69|# Composite systems
    70|psi_AB = tensor(psi_A, psi_B)  # Tensor product
    71|```
    72|
    73|**See** `references/core_concepts.md` for comprehensive coverage of quantum objects, states, operators, and tensor products.
    74|
    75|### 2. Time Evolution and Dynamics
    76|
    77|Multiple solvers for different scenarios:
    78|
    79|```python
    80|# Closed systems (unitary evolution)
    81|result = sesolve(H, psi0, tlist, e_ops=[num(N)])
    82|
    83|# Open systems (dissipation)
    84|c_ops = [np.sqrt(0.1) * destroy(N)]  # Collapse operators
    85|result = mesolve(H, psi0, tlist, c_ops, e_ops=[num(N)])
    86|
    87|# Quantum trajectories (Monte Carlo)
    88|result = mcsolve(H, psi0, tlist, c_ops, ntraj=500, e_ops=[num(N)])
    89|```
    90|
    91|**Solver selection guide:**
    92|- `sesolve`: Pure states, unitary evolution
    93|- `mesolve`: Mixed states, dissipation, general open systems
    94|- `mcsolve`: Quantum jumps, photon counting, individual trajectories
    95|- `brmesolve`: Weak system-bath coupling
    96|- `fmmesolve`: Time-periodic Hamiltonians (Floquet)
    97|
    98|**See** `references/time_evolution.md` for detailed solver documentation, time-dependent Hamiltonians, and advanced options.
    99|
   100|### 3. Analysis and Measurement
   101|
   102|Compute physical quantities:
   103|
   104|```python
   105|# Expectation values
   106|n_avg = expect(num(N), psi)
   107|
   108|# Entropy measures
   109|S = entropy_vn(rho)  # Von Neumann entropy
   110|C = concurrence(rho)  # Entanglement (two qubits)
   111|
   112|# Fidelity and distance
   113|F = fidelity(psi1, psi2)
   114|D = tracedist(rho1, rho2)
   115|
   116|# Correlation functions
   117|corr = correlation_2op_1t(H, rho0, taulist, c_ops, A, B)
   118|w, S = spectrum_correlation_fft(taulist, corr)
   119|
   120|# Steady states
   121|rho_ss = steadystate(H, c_ops)
   122|```
   123|
   124|**See** `references/analysis.md` for entropy, fidelity, measurements, correlation functions, and steady state calculations.
   125|
   126|### 4. Visualization
   127|
   128|Visualize quantum states and dynamics:
   129|
   130|```python
   131|# Bloch sphere
   132|b = Bloch()
   133|b.add_states(psi)
   134|b.show()
   135|
   136|# Wigner function (phase space)
   137|xvec = np.linspace(-5, 5, 200)
   138|W = wigner(psi, xvec, xvec)
   139|plt.contourf(xvec, xvec, W, 100, cmap='RdBu')
   140|
   141|# Fock distribution
   142|plot_fock_distribution(psi)
   143|
   144|# Matrix visualization
   145|hinton(rho)  # Hinton diagram
   146|matrix_histogram(H.full())  # 3D bars
   147|```
   148|
   149|**See** `references/visualization.md` for Bloch sphere animations, Wigner functions, Q-functions, and matrix visualizations.
   150|
   151|### 5. Advanced Methods
   152|
   153|Specialized techniques for complex scenarios:
   154|
   155|```python
   156|# Floquet theory (periodic Hamiltonians)
   157|T = 2 * np.pi / w_drive
   158|f_modes, f_energies = floquet_modes(H, T, args)
   159|result = fmmesolve(H, psi0, tlist, c_ops, T=T, args=args)
   160|
   161|# HEOM (non-Markovian, strong coupling)
   162|from qutip.nonmarkov.heom import HEOMSolver, BosonicBath
   163|bath = BosonicBath(Q, ck_real, vk_real)
   164|hsolver = HEOMSolver(H_sys, [bath], max_depth=5)
   165|result = hsolver.run(rho0, tlist)
   166|
   167|# Permutational invariance (identical particles)
   168|psi = dicke(N, j, m)  # Dicke states
   169|Jz = jspin(N, 'z')  # Collective operators
   170|```
   171|
   172|**See** `references/advanced.md` for Floquet theory, HEOM, permutational invariance, stochastic solvers, superoperators, and performance optimization.
   173|
   174|## Common Workflows
   175|
   176|### Simulating a Damped Harmonic Oscillator
   177|
   178|```python
   179|# System parameters
   180|N = 20  # Hilbert space dimension
   181|omega = 1.0  # Oscillator frequency
   182|kappa = 0.1  # Decay rate
   183|
   184|# Hamiltonian and collapse operators
   185|H = omega * num(N)
   186|c_ops = [np.sqrt(kappa) * destroy(N)]
   187|
   188|# Initial state
   189|psi0 = coherent(N, 3.0)
   190|
   191|# Time evolution
   192|tlist = np.linspace(0, 50, 200)
   193|result = mesolve(H, psi0, tlist, c_ops, e_ops=[num(N)])
   194|
   195|# Visualize
   196|plt.plot(tlist, result.expect[0])
   197|plt.xlabel('Time')
   198|plt.ylabel('⟨n⟩')
   199|plt.title('Photon Number Decay')
   200|plt.show()
   201|```
   202|
   203|### Two-Qubit Entanglement Dynamics
   204|
   205|```python
   206|# Create Bell state
   207|psi0 = bell_state('00')
   208|
   209|# Local dephasing on each qubit
   210|gamma = 0.1
   211|c_ops = [
   212|    np.sqrt(gamma) * tensor(sigmaz(), qeye(2)),
   213|    np.sqrt(gamma) * tensor(qeye(2), sigmaz())
   214|]
   215|
   216|# Track entanglement
   217|def compute_concurrence(t, psi):
   218|    rho = ket2dm(psi) if psi.isket else psi
   219|    return concurrence(rho)
   220|
   221|tlist = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
   222|result = mesolve(qeye([2, 2]), psi0, tlist, c_ops)
   223|
   224|# Compute concurrence for each state
   225|C_t = [concurrence(state.proj()) for state in result.states]
   226|
   227|plt.plot(tlist, C_t)
   228|plt.xlabel('Time')
   229|plt.ylabel('Concurrence')
   230|plt.title('Entanglement Decay')
   231|plt.show()
   232|```
   233|
   234|### Jaynes-Cummings Model
   235|
   236|```python
   237|# System parameters
   238|N = 10  # Cavity Fock space
   239|wc = 1.0  # Cavity frequency
   240|wa = 1.0  # Atom frequency
   241|g = 0.05  # Coupling strength
   242|
   243|# Operators
   244|a = tensor(destroy(N), qeye(2))  # Cavity
   245|sm = tensor(qeye(N), sigmam())  # Atom
   246|
   247|# Hamiltonian (RWA)
   248|H = wc * a.dag() * a + wa * sm.dag() * sm + g * (a.dag() * sm + a * sm.dag())
   249|
   250|# Initial state: cavity in coherent state, atom in ground state
   251|psi0 = tensor(coherent(N, 2), basis(2, 0))
   252|
   253|# Dissipation
   254|kappa = 0.1  # Cavity decay
   255|gamma = 0.05  # Atomic decay
   256|c_ops = [np.sqrt(kappa) * a, np.sqrt(gamma) * sm]
   257|
   258|# Observables
   259|n_cav = a.dag() * a
   260|n_atom = sm.dag() * sm
   261|
   262|# Evolve
   263|tlist = np.linspace(0, 50, 200)
   264|result = mesolve(H, psi0, tlist, c_ops, e_ops=[n_cav, n_atom])
   265|
   266|# Plot
   267|fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 6), sharex=True)
   268|axes[0].plot(tlist, result.expect[0])
   269|axes[0].set_ylabel('⟨n_cavity⟩')
   270|axes[1].plot(tlist, result.expect[1])
   271|axes[1].set_ylabel('⟨n_atom⟩')
   272|axes[1].set_xlabel('Time')
   273|plt.tight_layout()
   274|plt.show()
   275|```
   276|
   277|## Tips for Efficient Simulations
   278|
   279|1. **Truncate Hilbert spaces**: Use smallest dimension that captures dynamics
   280|2. **Choose appropriate solver**: `sesolve` for pure states is faster than `mesolve`
   281|3. **Time-dependent terms**: String format (e.g., `'cos(w*t)'`) is fastest
   282|4. **Store only needed data**: Use `e_ops` instead of storing all states
   283|5. **Adjust tolerances**: Balance accuracy with computation time via `Options`
   284|6. **Parallel trajectories**: `mcsolve` automatically uses multiple CPUs
   285|7. **Check convergence**: Vary `ntraj`, Hilbert space size, and tolerances
   286|
   287|## Troubleshooting
   288|
   289|**Memory issues**: Reduce Hilbert space dimension, use `store_final_state` option, or consider Krylov methods
   290|
   291|**Slow simulations**: Use string-based time-dependence, increase tolerances slightly, or try `method='bdf'` for stiff problems
   292|
   293|**Numerical instabilities**: Decrease time steps (`nsteps` option), increase tolerances, or check Hamiltonian/operators are properly defined
   294|
   295|**Import errors**: Ensure QuTiP is installed correctly; quantum gates require `qutip-qip` package
   296|
   297|## References
   298|
   299|This skill includes detailed reference documentation:
   300|
   301|- **`references/core_concepts.md`**: Quantum objects, states, operators, tensor products, composite systems
   302|- **`references/time_evolution.md`**: All solvers (sesolve, mesolve, mcsolve, brmesolve, etc.), time-dependent Hamiltonians, solver options
   303|- **`references/visualization.md`**: Bloch sphere, Wigner functions, Q-functions, Fock distributions, matrix plots
   304|- **`references/analysis.md`**: Expectation values, entropy, fidelity, entanglement measures, correlation functions, steady states
   305|- **`references/advanced.md`**: Floquet theory, HEOM, permutational invariance, stochastic methods, superoperators, performance tips
   306|
   307|## External Resources
   308|
   309|- Documentation: https://qutip.readthedocs.io/
   310|- Tutorials: https://qutip.org/qutip-tutorials/
   311|- API Reference: https://qutip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/apidoc/apidoc.html
   312|- GitHub: https://github.com/qutip/qutip
   313|", "total_lines": 312, "file_size": 9310, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

{"code": "from hermes_tools import terminal

script = r'''
import os
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np

from qutip import *
from qutip.piqs import *

# Output directory: /root (where the test searches)
output_dir = Path("/root")
print(f"Saving CSV files to {output_dir}")

# TLS parameters
N = 4
ntls = N
nds = num_dicke_states(ntls)
[jx, jy, jz] = jspin(N)
jp = jspin(N, "+")
jm = jp.dag()
w0 = 1
gE = 0.1
gD = 0.01
gP = 0.1
gCP = 0.1
gCE = 0.1
gCD = 0.1
h = w0 * jz

# photonic parameters
nphot = 16
wc = 1
kappa = 1
ratio_g = 2
g = ratio_g / np.sqrt(N)
a = destroy(nphot)

# TLS liouvillian - Case 1: local de-phasing & local pumping
system = Dicke(N=N)
system.hamiltonian = h
system.emission = 0
system.dephasing = gD
system.pumping = gP
system.collective_pumping = 0
system.collective_emission = 0
system.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv = system.liouvillian()

# TLS liouvillian - Case 2: local de-phasing & local emission
system2 = Dicke(N=N)
system2.hamiltonian = h
system2.emission = gE
system2.dephasing = gD
system2.pumping = 0
system2.collective_pumping = 0
system2.collective_emission = 0
system2.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv2 = system2.liouvillian()

# TLS liouvillian - Case 3: local de-phasing & local emission & collective pumping
system3 = Dicke(N=N)
system3.hamiltonian = h
system3.emission = gE
system3.dephasing = gD
system3.pumping = 0
system3.collective_pumping = gCP
system3.collective_emission = 0
system3.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv3 = system3.liouvillian()

# TLS liouvillian - Case 4: local de-phasing & local emission & collective emission
system4 = Dicke(N=N)
system4.hamiltonian = h
system4.emission = gE
system4.dephasing = gD
system4.pumping = 0
system4.collective_pumping = 0
system4.collective_emission = gCE
system4.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv4 = system4.liouvillian()

# photonic liouvillian
h_phot = wc * a.dag() * a
c_ops_phot = [np.sqrt(kappa) * a]
liouv_phot = liouvillian(h_phot, c_ops_phot)

# identity operators
id_tls = to_super(qeye(nds))
id_phot = to_super(qeye(nphot))

# light-matter superoperator
h_int = g * tensor(a + a.dag(), jx)
liouv_int = -1j * spre(h_int) + 1j * spost(h_int)

# total liouvillians
liouv_sum = super_tensor(liouv_phot, id_tls) + super_tensor(id_phot, liouv)
liouv_tot = liouv_sum + liouv_int

liouv_sum2 = super_tensor(liouv_phot, id_tls) + super_tensor(id_phot, liouv2)
liouv_tot2 = liouv_sum2 + liouv_int

liouv_sum3 = super_tensor(liouv_phot, id_tls) + super_tensor(id_phot, liouv3)
liouv_tot3 = liouv_sum3 + liouv_int

liouv_sum4 = super_tensor(liouv_phot, id_tls) + super_tensor(id_phot, liouv4)
liouv_tot4 = liouv_sum4 + liouv_int

# total operators
jz_tot = tensor(qeye(nphot), jz)
nphot_tot = tensor(a.dag() * a, qeye(nds))

# calculate steady states
rho_ss4 = steadystate(liouv_tot4, method="direct")
nphot_ss4 = expect(nphot_tot, rho_ss4)
psi4 = rho_ss4.ptrace(0)
print("Ensemble 4 is ok", nphot_ss4)

rho_ss = steadystate(liouv_tot, method="direct")
nphot_ss = expect(nphot_tot, rho_ss)
psi = rho_ss.ptrace(0)
print("Ensemble 1 is ok", nphot_ss)

rho_ss2 = steadystate(liouv_tot2, method="direct")
nphot_ss2 = expect(nphot_tot, rho_ss2)
psi2 = rho_ss2.ptrace(0)
print("Ensemble 2 is ok", nphot_ss2)

rho_ss3 = steadystate(liouv_tot3, method="direct")
nphot_ss3 = expect(nphot_tot, rho_ss3)
psi3 = rho_ss3.ptrace(0)
print("Ensemble 3 is ok", nphot_ss3)

# calculate Wigner function for photonic states
nx = 1000
xvec = np.linspace(-6, 6, nx)
W = wigner(psi, xvec, xvec)
print("1 ok")
W2 = wigner(psi2, xvec, xvec)
print("2 ok")
W3 = wigner(psi3, xvec, xvec)
print("3 ok")
W4 = wigner(psi4, xvec, xvec)
print("4 ok")

# Save each simulation result to its own CSV file
for idx, W_sim in enumerate([W, W2, W3, W4], start=1):
    out_path = output_dir / f"{idx}.csv"
    np.savetxt(out_path, W_sim, delimiter=",")
    print(f"Saved {out_path}")

print("All done!")
'''

r = terminal(command="cd /home/liangfeng/git/hermes-agent && source venv/bin/activate && python3 -c '$script'", timeout=600)
print(r)

gP = 0.1
gCP = 0.1
gCE = 0.1
gCD = 0.1
h = w0 * jz

# photonic parameters
nphot = 16
wc = 1
kappa = 1
ratio_g = 2
g = ratio_g / np.sqrt(N)
a = destroy(nphot)

# TLS liouvillian - Case 1: local de-phasing & local pumping
system = Dicke(N=N)
system.hamiltonian = h
system.emission = 0
system.dephasing = gD
system.pumping = gP
system.collective_pumping = 0
system.collective_emission = 0
system.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv = system.liouvillian()

# TLS liouvillian - Case 2: local de-phasing & local emission
system2 = Dicke(N=N)
system2.hamiltonian = h
system2.emission = gE
system2.dephasing = gD
system2.pumping = 0
system2.collective_pumping = 0
system2.collective_emission = 0
system2.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv2 = system2.liouvillian()

# TLS liouvillian - Case 3: local de-phasing & local emission & collective pumping
system3 = Dicke(N=N)
system3.hamiltonian = h
system3.emission = gE
system3.dephasing = gD
system3.pumping = 0
system3.collective_pumping = gCP
system3.collective_emission = 0
system3.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv3 = system3.liouvillian()

# TLS liouvillian - Case 4: local de-phasing & local emission & collective emission
system4 = Dicke(N=N)
system4.hamiltonian = h
system4.emission = gE
system4.dephasing = gD
system4.pumping = 0
system4.collective_pumping = 0
system4.collective_emission = gCE
system4.collective_dephasing = 0
liouv4 = system4.liouvillian()

# photonic liouvillian
h_phot = wc * a.dag() * a
c_ops_phot = [np.sqrt(kappa) * a]
liouv_phot = liouvillian(h_phot, c_ops_phot)

# identity operators
id_tls = to_super(qeye(nds))
id_phot = to_super(qeye(nphot))

# light-matter superoperator
h_int = g * tensor(a + a.dag(), jx)
liouv_int = -1j * spre(h_int) + 1j * spost(h_int)

# total liouvillians
liouv_sum = super_tensor(liouv_phot, id_tls) + super_tensor(id_phot, liouv)
liouv_tot = liouv_sum + liouv_int

liouv_sum2 = super_tensor(liouv_phot, id_tls) + super_tensor(id_phot, liouv2)

liouv_tot3 = liouv_sum3 + liouv_int

liouv_tot4 = liouv_sum4 + liouv_int

# total operators
jz_tot = tensor(qeye(nphot), jz)

psi3 = rho_ss3.ptrace(0)
print("Ensemble 3 is ok", nphot_ss3)

print("1 ok")

print("2 ok")
W3 = wigner(psi3, xvec, xvec)
print("3 ok")
W4 = wigner(psi4, xvec, xvec)
print("4 ok")

    np.savetxt(out_path, W_sim, delimiter=",")

# SkillsBench

Benchmark for evaluating how well AI agents use skills. 89 tasks, working toward 100+.

## Python environment (Hermes monorepo)

This directory is a **nested Python package** (`skillsbench` in `pyproject.toml`; `requires-python >= 3.12`). Hermes itself supports Python 3.11+, but use **3.12+** when developing or running BenchFlow workflows here.

- **Same venv as Hermes, BenchFlow only:** from the Hermes repo root, `pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"` (or `uv pip install -e ".[skillsbench]"`). That pulls in `benchflow` via the root `hermes-agent` optional extra; it does not install the `skillsbench` package in editable mode.
- **Full subproject:** `cd benchmark/skillsbench` then `pip install -e .` or `uv sync` (see `pyproject.toml` for dev groups and `uv` sources).

## Commands

```bash
pip install benchflow>=0.3.0a7
bench tasks init <task-name>
bench tasks check tasks/<task-id>
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a oracle
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp -s tasks/<task-id>/environment/skills/  # with skills
bench eval create -t tasks/<task-id> -a claude-agent-acp  # without skills
bench job -t tasks/ -a claude-agent-acp -e daytona -c 8
bench metrics jobs/<run-dir>
bench skills list
bench skills eval --help
```

## Task Layout

```
tasks/<task-id>/
  instruction.md          # Human-written. Outcome-focused. No skill hints.
  task.toml               # Metadata, timeouts, resources
  environment/
    Dockerfile            # Container setup
    skills/               # Domain skills (generalizable, not task-specific)
  solution/
    solve.sh              # Oracle (human-written, derives answers via computation)
  tests/
    test.sh               # Pytest runner, writes reward.txt
    test_outputs.py       # Outcome-based assertions
```

## Rules

- instruction.md, solve.sh, and task.toml must be human-written — never generate these
- Never mention skill names in instructions
- Skills must be generalizable and reusable, not task-specific
- Tests verify outcomes, not process — don't check which tools were used
- Oracle must derive answers through computation, not hardcode them
- No fake scenarios, no synthetic data when real data exists
- Prefer tasks without external API dependencies

## Key References

- [../../AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) — Hermes repo guide; **Development Environment → SkillsBench: Hermes batch driver** documents `benchmark/scripts/run_skillsbench_with_hermes.py` (defaults, examples, flags).
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — full contributor guide, rubrics, authorship policy
- [rubrics/](rubrics/) — task proposal and implementation review criteria
- [.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md) — how to write skills
- [docs/unit-test-guidelines.md](docs/unit-test-guidelines.md) — test statistics and patterns

    20|def load_json(filepath):
    21|    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
    22|        return json.load(f)
    23|
    24|
    25|def get_true_reference(time, config):
    26|    """Compute ground truth reference at given time from system_config.json."""
    27|    step_time = config["step_time"]
    28|    T_ref_initial = np.array(config["T_ref_initial"])
    29|    T_ref_final = np.array(config["T_ref_final"])
    30|
    31|    if time < step_time:
    32|        return T_ref_initial
    33|    else:
    34|        return T_ref_final
    35|
    36|
    37|def compute_true_jacobian(x, config):
    38|    """Compute ground truth linearized A, B matrices from dynamics equations."""
    39|    EA = config["EA"]
    40|    J = config["J"]
    41|    R = config["R"]
    42|    fb = config["fb"]
    43|    L = config["L"]
    44|    dt = config["dt"]
    45|    num_sec = 6
    46|
    47|    df_dx = np.zeros((12, 12))
    48|    df_du = np.zeros((12, 6))
    49|
    50|    for i in range(num_sec):
    51|        v = x[i + num_sec]
    52|        T = x[i]
    53|
    54|        # Tension row derivatives: dT_i/dt = (EA/L)*(v_i - v_{i-1}) + (1/L)*(v_{i-1}*T_{i-1} - v_i*T_i)
    55|        df_dx[i, i] = -v / L
    56|        df_dx[i, i + num_sec] = EA / L - T / L
    57|        if i > 0:
    58|            vm = x[i + num_sec - 1]
    59|            Tm = x[i - 1]
    60|            df_dx[i, i - 1] = vm / L
    61|            df_dx[i, i + num_sec - 1] = -EA / L + Tm / L
    62|
    63|        # Velocity row derivatives: dv_i/dt = (R^2/J)*(T_{i+1} - T_i) + (R/J)*u_i - (fb/J)*v_i
    64|        df_dx[i + num_sec, i] = -R**2 / J
    65|        df_dx[i + num_sec, i + num_sec] = -fb / J
    66|        if i < num_sec - 1:
    67|            df_dx[i + num_sec, i + 1] = R**2 / J
    68|        df_du[i + num_sec, i] = R / J
    69|
    70|    # Discretize using Euler method
    71|    A_d = np.eye(12) + dt * df_dx
    72|    B_d = dt * df_du
    73|    return A_d, B_d

     7|#!/usr/bin/env python3
     8|"""
     9|Oracle solution for R2R MPC Control task.
    10|
    11|This script:
    12|1. Designs MPC controller (horizon, costs, LQR gain)
    13|2. Runs closed-loop simulation with finite-horizon LQR
    14|3. Calculates performance metrics
    15|"""
    16|
    17|import json
    18|import numpy as np
    19|from scipy import linalg
    20|from r2r_simulator import R2RSimulator
    21|
    22|
    23|def compute_jacobian(x, params):
    24|    """
    25|    Compute linearized A, B matrices at given state.
    26|    Derived from dynamics equations:
    27|        dT_i/dt = (EA/L)*(v_i - v_{i-1}) + (1/L)*(v_{i-1}*T_{i-1} - v_i*T_i)
    28|        dv_i/dt = (R^2/J)*(T_{i+1} - T_i) + (R/J)*u_i - (fb/J)*v_i
    29|    """
    30|    EA, J, R, fb, L = params["EA"], params["J"], params["R"], params["fb"], params["L"]
    31|    dt = params["dt"]
    32|    num_sec = 6
    33|
    34|    df_dx = np.zeros((12, 12))
    35|    df_du = np.zeros((12, 6))
    36|
    37|    for i in range(num_sec):
    38|        v = x[i + num_sec]
    39|        T = x[i]
    40|
    41|        # Tension row derivatives
    42|        df_dx[i, i] = -v / L                           # d/dT_i
    43|        df_dx[i, i + num_sec] = EA / L - T / L         # d/dv_i
    44|        if i > 0:
    45|            vm = x[i + num_sec - 1]
    46|            Tm = x[i - 1]
    47|            df_dx[i, i - 1] = vm / L                    # d/dT_{i-1}
    48|            df_dx[i, i + num_sec - 1] = -EA / L + Tm / L  # d/dv_{i-1}
    49|
    50|        # Velocity row derivatives
    51|        df_dx[i + num_sec, i] = -R**2 / J              # d/dT_i
    52|        df_dx[i + num_sec, i + num_sec] = -fb / J      # d/dv_i
    53|        if i < num_sec - 1:
    54|            df_dx[i + num_sec, i + 1] = R**2 / J       # d/dT_{i+1}
    55|        df_du[i + num_sec, i] = R / J                  # d/du_i
    56|
    57|    # Discretize using Euler method
    58|    A_d = np.eye(12) + dt * df_dx
    59|    B_d = dt * df_du
    60|    return A_d, B_d
    61|
    62|
    63|def compute_lqr_gain(A, B, Q, R, dt):
    64|    """Compute LQR gain using continuous-time ARE."""
    65|    # Convert discrete to approximate continuous
    66|    A_c = (A - np.eye(12)) / dt
    67|    B_c = B / dt
    68|    P = linalg.solve_continuous_are(A_c, B_c, Q, R)
    69|    K = np.linalg.solve(R, B_c.T @ P)
    70|    return K
    71|
    72|
    73|def design_controller(sim):
    74|    """Design MPC controller parameters."""
    75|    params = sim.get_params()
    76|    x_ref, _ = sim.get_reference(0)
    77|    A, B = compute_jacobian(x_ref, params)
    78|
    79|    T_ref = 30.0
    80|    v0 = 0.01
    81|
    82|    Q_diag = np.concatenate([

    84|        1e-1 * np.ones(6) / v0**2
    85|    ])
    86|    R_diag = 3.33e-2 * np.ones(6)
    87|
    88|    Q = np.diag(Q_diag)
    89|    R = np.diag(R_diag)
    90|
    91|    K_lqr = compute_lqr_gain(A, B, Q, R, sim.dt)
    92|
    93|    return {
    94|        "horizon_N": 9,
    95|        "Q_diag": Q_diag.tolist(),
    96|        "R_diag": R_diag.tolist(),
    97|        "K_lqr": K_lqr.tolist(),
    98|        "A_matrix": A.tolist(),
    99|        "B_matrix": B.tolist()
   100|    }
   101|
   102|
   103|def finite_horizon_lqr(A, B, Q, R, N, x0):

   106|    K = np.zeros((nu, nx, N - 1))

   110|    for k in range(N - 2, -1, -1):

   112|        Pk = Q + A.T @ Pk @ (A - B @ K[:, :, k])
   113|
   114|    # Return first control
   115|    return -K[:, :, 0] @ x0
   116|
   117|
   118|def run_control_loop(sim, controller_params, duration=5.0):
   119|    """Run closed-loop MPC control."""
   120|    sim.reset()
   121|    params = sim.get_params()
   122|    dt = params["dt"]
   123|    num_sec = 6
   124|
   125|    Q = np.diag(controller_params["Q_diag"])
   126|    R = np.diag(controller_params["R_diag"])
   127|    K_lqr = np.array(controller_params["K_lqr"])
   128|    N = controller_params["horizon_N"]
   129|
   130|    control_data = []
   131|    c_I = 0.3       # Integral gain
   132|    gamma = 0.95    # Integral decay
   133|    u_I = np.zeros(num_sec)
   134|
   135|    for step_num in range(int(duration / dt)):
   136|        x = sim.get_state()
   137|        x_ref, u_ref = sim.get_reference()

   139|        # Get linearized model at current reference
   140|        A, B = compute_jacobian(x_ref, params)
   141|
   142|        # Compute MPC control via finite-horizon LQR
   143|        dx = x - x_ref
   144|        du = finite_horizon_lqr(A, B, Q, R, N, dx)
   145|
   146|        # Add integral action for offset-free tracking
   147|        u_I = gamma * u_I - c_I * dt * (x[:num_sec] - x_ref[:num_sec])
   148|
   149|        # Total control: reference + MPC deviation + LQR feedback + integral
   150|        u = u_ref + du - K_lqr @ dx + u_I

   153|        sim.step(u)

   155|        control_data.append({

   169|    refs = np.array([d["references"][:6] for d in control_data])
   170|    times = np.array([d["time"] for d in control_data])

   174|    # Steady-state error (last 20%)
